member.name: M:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.DataModelling.TypePropertyInfo.CompareDefaultValue(System.Object,System.Object,ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.SupportedEsriFieldType)
member.summary: The CIM objects use json serialization which does not differentiate the numeric types (int 32, int 64). The type property has a default value of type object which means C# numeric types are boxed. When deserialized all int types become 64 bit types which interferes with the value comparison. This comparison casts the default values to the specific field type and performs the comparison.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.KnowledgeGraphModule.RunCommandWithAutoRefreshDataModel``1(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Func{ArcGIS.Desktop.Framework.Threading.Tasks.CancelableProgressor,``0})
member.summary:
This function runs a command and refreshes the datamodel and reruns the command if the command error suggests that the Data Model may need a refresh.
If there are continuous changes to the Data Model and the KG that require an update, the command may rerun the command and refresh the Data Model many times.
member.param: The command function to execute. It is assumed that on error, this function throws an exception.

member.summary: Returns whether the specified item is capable of having child items.
member.returns: true if the specified item is capable of having child items; otherwise, false.
member.remarks:
The default implementation of this method returns true. This method should only return false if an item is not capable of having child items and is always a 'leaf' node in the tree. It should not return false if the item can have child items, but doesn't at the current time.
Optimizations are in place to not call when this method returns true. This method should be overridden if is used and certain items are known to be 'leaf' nodes.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.DomainHelper.ExtractAndUpdateDomain(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.List{esriGeoDatabase.IGraphProperty})
member.summary: Updates the domain data for the specified type by processing a list of graph properties.
member.remarks: This method ensures that the domain data for the specified type is updated based on the provided graph properties. If a property has a valid domain, it is added or updated in the domain data. If a property does not have a domain, it is removed from the domain data if it exists. The operation is thread-safe.
member.param: The name of the type whose domain data is to be updated. Cannot be or empty.
A list of graph properties to process. Each property may contribute to the domain data for the specified type. Cannot be and must contain at least one element.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.DomainHelper.GetDomainInformation(System.String)
member.summary: Retrieves domain information for the specified type.
member.remarks: This method is thread-safe. If the specified does not exist in the domain map, the method returns an empty dictionary instead of null.
member.param: The type of domain information to retrieve. Cannot be null or empty.
member.returns: A dictionary containing domain information associated with the specified type. If the type is not found or is null/empty, an empty dictionary is returned.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.DomainHelper.Clear
member.summary: Clears all entries from the domain map.
member.remarks: This method removes all key-value pairs from the internal domain map. It is thread-safe and ensures that the operation is performed atomically.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.DomainDataHolder
member.summary: Represents a holder for domain-related data, including coded value domains and range domains.
member.remarks: This class provides properties and methods to manage domain information, such as domain name, owner, description, data type, and domain-specific values. It supports both coded value domains and range domains. Use the method to configure the domain properties based on a provided domain object.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.DomainDataHolder.InitializeDomain(esriGeoDatabase.IDomain)
member.summary: Initializes the domain properties based on the provided domain object.
member.remarks: This method configures the domain properties, such as name, owner, description, and data type, based on the type of the provided domain. If the domain is a coded value domain, the method populates the list of coded values. If the domain is a range domain, the method sets the minimum and maximum values. Unsupported domain types are handled by resetting all domain-specific properties to their default values.
member.param: The domain object to initialize from. This can be a coded value domain or a range domain.

When the cost value is defined via a property, negative property values are replaced by zero and null property values are replaced by the default cost value.
Relationship cost is used by shortest path based measures: Betweeness, Closeness and Harmonic centrality algorithms..

Relationship importance is used by Degree, Eigenvector and PageRank centrality algorithms..

member.summary:

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.ActiproPopupAutoCloseBehavior
member.summary: Actipro popup button closes automatically if content is clicked. To prevent it from closing the property StaysOpen has to be set to true. It still closes when the popup loses focus, but only when it was clicked at least once. I consider it as a bug, to avoid that, this attached property refreshes the muse capture and it closes without clicking. If there are checkboxes for some options within the popup, and the user activates it with keyboard navigation, the focus is lost to some arbitrary location on the main layer in pro. This also seems to be a bug. Therefore this case is handled as well in this attached property.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.ComboBoxAutoOpenBehavior
member.summary: If used inside a datagrid, the combobox will open its drop down and sets focus on its textbox. Properties like DropDownOpenInitially and IsDropDown open have to be set to true, otherwise focus is lost. EnsureTextBox focus does not work as expected for ExtendedComboBox. In addition if combobox visibility is collapsed or hidden, the datagrid renders the combobox and the popup still shows up. This is also intercepted.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.ComboBoxPreventClosingOnExpanderClickBehavior.Popup_PreviewMouseDown(System.Object,System.Windows.Input.MouseButtonEventArgs)
member.summary: Check whether a toggle button is up the call chain. Toggle its state and set the event to handled, set that tag to true to mark the popup as 'expanded/collapsed by expander' click. The popup when it shows a vertical scrollbar, seems to close the expander and closes the popup on mouseup. This is triggered on the wrong visual item as the scrollbar disappears on collapse. member.summary: Edit mode has to be triggered by mouse down, mouse up is too late as DataGrid would interfere with its own mousedown. The centrality configuration: a binary serialization of a CIMKnowledgeGraphCentralityConfiguration.

The subgraph: a binary serialization of a CIMKnowledgeGraphSubGraph. Centrality algorithms will only take into account entities and relationships of the subgraph, and only compute scores for entites of the subgraph.

Out array of size centralityMeasures.size() * subGraphEntities.externalIndexToUID.size() containing the centrality scores for each centrality measure and for each entity. member.name: F:ArcGIS.Desktop.Internal.KnowledgeGraph.FindPathsErrors.configurationTooComplexErrorMessage
member.summary:
When this string is non-empty, the configuration is "too complex" and the string content explains how the configuration complexity was computed and how users can reduce the complexity by changing the configuration.
The explanation says that the formula used for computing the configuration complexity is:
complexity = 2^n_mandatory_bidirectional_relationship_waypoints * n_mandatory_waypoints! * (n_mandatory_waypoints + 2)
and the maximum allowed complexity is 2'540'000'000.
To reduce the complexity users can: - convert mandatory bidirectional relationship waypoints to unidirectional relationship waypoints by adding a directionality constraint on the corresponding relationship type, - reduce the count of mandatory (entity or relationship) waypoints.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Desktop.KnowledgeGraph.KnowledgeGraphDataModelView
member.summary: Represents the data model view of a Knowledge Graph investigation in a pane.

remarks.para: A project can contain multiple investigations. An data model view is simply a view of an investigation. The KnowledgeGraphDataModelView class provides methods and properties to navigate and interact with items in the investigation.

There can be multiple data model views open at a given time, but there can only be one active data model view. The active data model view will set the context for the ribbon and many of the dock panes in the application. For example, the Contents pane will reflect the items of the active data model view's investigation. The instance of the active data model view can be accessed via the static the property. The property will return null if there is no active data model view.

The data model view also provides the context for managing selected items in the Contents pane. For example, the method returns a collection of entities that are currently selected in the Contents pane.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Desktop.KnowledgeGraph.KnowledgeGraphInvestigation
member.summary: Represents a Knowledge Graph investigation in a project and provides access to the entities, relationships and other items in the knowledge graph.

remarks.para: To create a KnowledgeGraphInvestigation, you must call a create method of the KnowledgeGraphInvestigationFactory class.
To open a KnowledgeGraphInvestigation, use the ProApp.Panes.CreateInvestigationPane method.

You need to use a KnowledgeGraphInvestigationView to interact with a KnowledgeGraphInvestigation. Multiple KnowledgeGraphInvestigationViews can be opened for a KnowledgeGraphInvestigation at a given time, but there can only be one active KnowledgeGraphInvestigationView which is returned by the KnowledgeGraphInvestigation.Active static member. Use the KnowledgeGraphInvestigation property to access the KnowledgeGraphInvestigation object associated with the KnowledgeGraphInvestigationView.

member.name: T:ArcGIS.Desktop.KnowledgeGraph.KnowledgeGraphInvestigationView
member.summary: Represents the view of a Knowledge Graph investigation in a pane.

remarks.para: A project can contain multiple investigations. An investigation view is simply a view of an investigation. The KnowledgeGraphInvestigationView class provides methods and properties to navigate and interact with items in the investigation. The investigation being visualized in the view can be accessed via the property.

There can be multiple investigation views open at a given time, but there can only be one active investigation view. The active investigation view will set the context for the ribbon and many of the dock panes in the application. For example, the Contents pane will reflect the items of the active investigation view's investigation. The instance of the active investigation view can be accessed via the static the property. The property will return null if there is no active investigation view.

The investigation view also provides the context for managing selected items in the Contents pane. For example, the method returns a collection of entities that are currently selected in the Contents pane.

member.name: M:ArcGIS.Desktop.Mapping.KnowledgeGraphExtensions.ApplySchemaEdits(ArcGIS.Core.Data.Knowledge.KnowledgeGraph,ArcGIS.Core.Data.DDL.SchemaBuilder)
member.summary: Addins should use the knowledge graph ApplySchemaEdits() call to execute enqueued schema operations on rather than . This method must be called on the MCT. Use QueuedTask.Run.
member.param: The knowledge graph "this" extension method parameter
The schema builder with the enqueued operations to be executed
member.remarks:
To ensure proper refresh of the application UI when making schema changes to a knowledge graph, instead of calling schemaBuilder.Build(), addins should instead execute the enqueued schema operations with a kg.ApplySchemaEdits(schemaBuilder) call. This ensures that the map, link chart, or investigation UI (whichever is active) will refresh correctly after the schema edits have been applied.
Schema operations will fail if ApplySchemaEdits is called whenever an edit session is active on the knowledge graph.
Schema edits will still be applied if an addin uses schemaBuilder.Build() but the application UI may be inconsistent after the schema edits have been completed and need to be manually refreshed, or, in some cases, the active view or even project, closed and re-opened.
member.returns: true if the schema edits were successfully applied.
member.exception: schemaBuilder cannot be null
